newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-43 PER CENT OF FRENCH SAY FRANCE TO WIN WORLD CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-43 PER CENT OF FRENCH SAY FRANCE TO WIN WORLD CUP.

text.p: Almost one in every two Frenchmen believes France will win the World Cup next year, according to a national poll to be published on Sunday.

The Journal de Dimanche poll also found that David Ginola was the player most Frenchmen wanted to see in the national team, although the Tottenham Hotspur winger has not been selected for nearly two years.

The poll showed 43 per cent of French people believe France will win the World Cup for the first time when they host the 1998 finals between June 10 and July 12. Ten per cent less believe France will not win the tournament and 23 per cent abstained.
The poll included 1,061 people aged from 15 upwards.

Former captain Jean-Pierre Papin, like Ginola out of coach Aime Jacquet's picture for two years, won the third highest number of votes behind Monaco goalkeeper Fabien Barthez when those polled were asked for their top three players.
Among people polled who expressed a keen interest in football, Barthez won most votes ahead of Youri Djorkaeff of Inter Milan. Ginola was fourth, Bordeaux striker Papin 10th.

Djorkaeff, who has been capped 29 times and scored 15 goals for France, was the player named most times in an ideal team of 14 including three substitutes both by all the people polled and by those interested in football.
